cls: Haematopoietic agent - recombinant granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF)
pharm: Recombinant human G-CSF that binds receptors on neutrophil precursors to stimulate their proliferation, differentiation, survival and release into the circulation, and enhances mature neutrophil function
quick: 5 mcg/kg/day SC or IV with chemotherapy; 10 mcg/kg/day for BMT or PBPC mobilisation
Limited data; use only if clearly needed
Likely minimal transfer; considered compatible with caution
CBC/ANC, spleen size, signs of splenic rupture/ARDS/capillary leak
summary: Filgrastim is a recombinant human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor (G-CSF) that raises neutrophil counts. It is used to reduce febrile neutropenia in patients on myelosuppressive chemotherapy, to shorten neutropenia after AML induction/consolidation and after bone-marrow transplant, to mobilise autologous peripheral-blood progenitor cells for collection, and for severe chronic neutropenia. The usual chemotherapy dose is 5 mcg/kg/day subcutaneously or IV; 10 mcg/kg/day is used for transplant and progenitor-cell mobilisation. Key risks include splenic rupture, acute respiratory distress syndrome, serious allergic reactions, capillary leak syndrome and (in sickle-cell disease) sickle-cell crises.
indications: Decrease the incidence of infection (febrile neutropenia) in non-myeloid malignancy patients receiving myelosuppressive chemotherapy
Reduce time to neutrophil recovery and duration of fever after induction/consolidation chemotherapy for acute myeloid leukaemia
Reduce duration of neutropenia and sequelae in patients undergoing myeloablative chemotherapy followed by bone-marrow transplantation
Mobilise autologous haematopoietic progenitor cells into peripheral blood for leukapheresis collection
Chronic administration to reduce infection in symptomatic congenital, cyclic or idiopathic severe chronic neutropenia
Increase survival in patients acutely exposed to myelosuppressive doses of radiation (haematopoietic acute radiation syndrome)

dosage.d: 5 mcg/kg/day by SC injection, short IV infusion (15-30 min) or continuous IV infusion
dosage.t: Daily until expected neutrophil nadir is passed and ANC recovers
dosage.n: Start at least 24 h after cytotoxic chemotherapy; do not give 24 h before or after

dosage.d: 10 mcg/kg/day as an IV infusion of no longer than 24 hours
dosage.n: First dose at least 24 h after chemotherapy and bone-marrow infusion

dosage.t: At least 4 days before first leukapheresis, continued until last leukapheresis

dosage.d: Congenital: 6 mcg/kg SC twice daily; idiopathic/cyclic: 5 mcg/kg SC once daily (starting doses)
dosage.n: Titrate to clinical response and ANC

dosage.t: Begin as soon as possible after suspected exposure; continue until ANC recovers
dosage.n: Estimate absorbed radiation dose where possible

admin: Give by subcutaneous injection or intravenous infusion as per indication
Do not administer within 24 hours before or after cytotoxic chemotherapy
Allow refrigerated product to reach room temperature before injection; do not shake
Discard if discoloured or particulate matter is present; the prefilled syringe needle cap may contain natural rubber latex
Monitor complete blood counts to guide duration and avoid excessive leucocytosis
moa: Filgrastim is recombinant methionyl human granulocyte colony-stimulating factor produced in E. coli. It binds to specific cell-surface G-CSF receptors on haematopoietic cells, stimulating proliferation, differentiation and commitment of neutrophil progenitors and release of mature neutrophils from the bone marrow into the blood. It also enhances neutrophil functions such as phagocytosis and antibody-dependent killing. Because it is lineage-specific for the neutrophil line, it has minimal effect on other blood cells.

absolute: Known serious hypersensitivity to filgrastim products or E. coli-derived proteins
relative: Sickle-cell trait or disease (risk of severe sickle-cell crises)
Myeloid malignancy where stimulation of tumour growth is a concern
Concurrent use during the 24-hour periods around cytotoxic chemotherapy
monitor: Left upper-quadrant or shoulder-tip pain (splenic enlargement/rupture)
Signs of capillary leak syndrome (oedema, hypotension, haemoconcentration)

preg: There are limited human data. Filgrastim crosses the placenta. Animal studies showed adverse effects at high doses. Use during pregnancy only if the potential benefit justifies the potential risk to the fetus.
lact: Endogenous G-CSF is a normal milk component and filgrastim is a large protein unlikely to be absorbed intact by the infant. It is generally considered compatible with breastfeeding when treatment is indicated; use with caution.
renal: No dose adjustment is required in renal impairment.
hepatic: No dose adjustment is required in hepatic impairment.

major: Concurrent cytotoxic chemotherapy within 24 h before or after - rapidly dividing myeloid cells are sensitive to chemotherapy; avoid overlap
moderate: Lithium - may potentiate the release of neutrophils; monitor neutrophil counts
Other myeloid growth factors - additive effects
minor: May transiently affect imaging of bone (increased haematopoietic activity)
interactions.diagnostics: Increased haematopoietic marrow activity can produce transient positive bone-imaging findings; monitor CBC/ANC

serious: Sickle-cell crises in patients with sickle-cell disorders
rare: Myelodysplasia/AML in severe chronic neutropenia (long-term, congenital)
emergency: Left upper-quadrant/shoulder pain - possible splenic rupture
Acute dyspnoea/hypoxia - ARDS or alveolar haemorrhage
Capillary leak syndrome with hypotension and haemoconcentration

monitoring: Complete blood count and ANC at regular intervals (more often around the nadir)
Spleen size and left upper-quadrant/shoulder-tip pain
Blood pressure, oedema and haematocrit (capillary leak)
Urinalysis/renal function with proteinuria or haematuria (glomerulonephritis)
counsel: Bone or muscle aches are common; simple analgesics usually help
Seek urgent care for pain in the upper-left abdomen or tip of the shoulder (possible spleen problem)
Report breathlessness, fever or swelling promptly
Report rash, swelling of face/throat or difficulty breathing (allergic reaction)
If self-injecting, follow the technique you were taught, rotate sites, and do not shake the syringe; allow it to reach room temperature first
Keep all blood-test appointments so the dose and duration can be adjusted
pk: Neutrophil count begins to rise within hours; an early transient dip may precede the rise
ANC typically peaks within 3-5 days of starting daily dosing
Neutrophil counts return toward baseline within about 1-7 days after stopping
Refrigerate at 2-8 C, protect from light, do not freeze or shake; brief room-temperature excursions allowed per label
pearls: Do not give within 24 hours before or after cytotoxic chemotherapy
Investigate left upper-quadrant or shoulder-tip pain for splenic rupture
Watch for ARDS, capillary leak syndrome and serious allergic reactions
Avoid or use with great caution in sickle-cell disease (crisis risk)
No dose adjustment needed for renal or hepatic impairment
Monitor CBC to avoid excessive leucocytosis and to time discontinuation
missed: If a scheduled dose is missed, contact the treating team; depending on timing it may be given as soon as remembered, but do not give two doses close together. Doses must not fall within 24 hours of chemotherapy.
overdose: Overdose produces excessive leucocytosis. There is no specific antidote; discontinue or reduce the dose and monitor blood counts. Leucapheresis may be considered for extreme leucocytosis with symptoms.
